transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-23
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Elena (Redwood CSM), Tom (Redwood SE), Jared (HoloMart Head of ML), Priya (Platform), Marco (CTO), Sofia (DevOps), Asha (PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Quick QBR focusing on recent spike during promotional campaign, cost anomalies, proposals for Dedicated pilot, and security checklist.

--- Topics ---
1) Cost spike after June promo
2) Tail latency affecting home page recommendations
3) Pilot scope: Dedicated capacity + VPC private control plane
4) Compliance docs and keystore/KMS questions
5) Benchmark and next steps

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining on short notice, um let's do quick roll call. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood.
[00:06] Jared Kim: Hey Maya, Jared here. Sorry for the slight delay, had a quick stand.
[00:09] Priya Singh: Priya from HoloMart platform.
[00:11] Marco Silva: Marco, CTO.
[00:12] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, DevOps.
[00:14] Asha Rao: Asha, PM.
[00:16] Ravi Patel: Ravi, Redwood SE.
[00:18] Elena Ortiz: Elena, CSM.
[00:20] Tom Bowers: Tom, solutions engineering.

[01:02] Maya Chen: Cool. Quick agenda: retrospective on June promo spike, go over cost drivers and tail latency, talk pilot options (Dedicated / Private), security checklist, and agree next steps. Sound good?
[01:12] Marco Silva: Yes, please. We're mostly concerned about the June 18 campaign where spend jumped unexpectedly and a few percent of recommendations timed out.

[02:05] Priya Singh: To add detail — our normal token usage is about 120M tokens/day, but during the promo we saw sustained bursts pushing to 220M for ~12 hours. The billing looked non-linear, and our infra team reported tail p99 latency up from ~320ms to ~980ms on a subset of routes.
[02:22] Ravi Patel: Right, that aligns with our telemetry. The p99 regression during sustained bursts is often down to batching backpressure and cache cold-start behavior, we saw KV cache churn on the session keys.

[03:05] Sofia Alvarez: There were also a couple infra-level retries from our side; we didn't instrument prefix caching fully so cache misses were high. But the billing anomaly — looks like rounding + tokenization differences played a part?
[03:20] Tom Bowers: Billing can be impacted by sequence length distribution. When the input sequences spike, effective per-request token counts increase and batching gets less efficient, so unit cost goes up non-linearly. Also if retries happen we double-count.

[04:10] Jared Kim: Can Redwood’s platform mitigate that without us refactoring the client? We need practical levers.
[04:18] Ravi Patel: Yes — three levers: 1) smart routing to focused Dedicated pool during promos, 2) prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated decoding, and 3) quantized model variants for high-throughput non-critical endpoints. For near-term we can recommend a Dedicated pilot for promotional windows.

[05:01] Marco Silva: We're interested in Dedicated but need to understand predictable cost. Is there a clear cost per throughput metric we can commit to?
[05:10] Maya Chen: We can provide commitment tiers: reserved GPUs for baseline throughput, plus burstable credit for peaks. We'll send a tiered pricing spreadsheet. That was one of the next steps agreed.

[06:00] Priya Singh: On security: we operate in EMEA and need data residency and key control, plus SOC2 compliance evidence. If we do Private (VPC) deploy, how mature is the control plane isolation?
[06:15] Elena Ortiz: Redwood Private provides customer-managed VPC with optional on-prem packages; we integrate with KMS and HSM providers and provide audit logs. We'll share the SOC2 pack and a network architecture doc.

[07:08] Sofia Alvarez: Do you support customer-managed KMS keys for model data / logs? We need to ensure we can rotate keys and that logs don't leak PII out-of-band.
[07:18] Ravi Patel: Yes, we support KMS integration with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own HSM options in Private deployments. Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM. Note: some telemetry still needs to cross control-plane channels for metrics; we can provide redaction options.

[08:22] Asha Rao: Coming back to success criteria — we want p95 < 200ms, p99 < 700ms, and cost per 1M requests under $X (we'll define X after reviewing your pilot pricing).
[08:35] Maya Chen: Sounds fair. We'll help define the target $X based on traffic profile.

[09:10] Marco Silva: For the pilot, we want to scope it to 2 weeks of real traffic with a shadow mode and then an active run during a smaller promo. Is that realistic?
[09:19] Ravi Patel: Yes — common pattern: 1 week of shadow/observability to tune batching and caching, then 1 week active with controlled traffic ramp. We'll supply test harness and a replay plan.

[10:02] Priya Singh: We can produce 7 days of traffic trace and a representative sample of top endpoints, but we need guidance on what to capture.
[10:12] Sofia Alvarez: We'll capture request size histograms, session id distributions, sequence length CDFs, and error/retry rates.

[11:00] Tom Bowers: For the benchmark, we'll run two model variants: a high-accurate FP16-ish model and a quantized int8 variant to compare cost/latency tradeoffs. That should show where quantization is acceptable.

[12:05] Jared Kim: About rollouts: if the Dedicated path performs well, how long to move to production at scale? We're thinking ~8 weeks to include validation, SRE runbooks, and SSO integration.
[12:18] Maya Chen: That's reasonable. The Dedicated onboarding itself ~2–3 weeks for capacity provisioning and baseline tests, then integration and runbook can be 4–6 weeks depending on your SSO and approval cycles.

[13:00] Priya Singh: There's a specific concern about tokenization differences — we saw ~1–2% token count delta between our local tokenizer and Redwood's hosting tokenizer which led to some surprise billing. Can that be normalized?
[13:11] Ravi Patel: We can run a tokenizer parity check during the benchmark; if necessary we can pin a specific tokenizer version and produce a reconciliation sheet. Also we support reporting by input/response tokens per-route to make audits easier.

[14:05] Marco Silva: Any thoughts on autoscaling behavior? Our infra team prefers predictable capacity rather than wide autoscale swings that change latency.
[14:16] Tom Bowers: Dedicated offers predictable baseline with controlled autoscale windows. You can configure autoscaling policies by policy: latency SLOs and cost caps. We can set conservative autoscale thresholds for production.

[15:00] Sofia Alvarez: On the practical side: if we go Private VPC, will Redwood still host the control plane or do we run that entirely in our account?
[15:10] Elena Ortiz: We offer two Private modes: 1) customer-managed VPC where the control plane endpoints are reachable only within your VPC, but Redwood still manages the control plane software; or 2) full on-prem package for air-gapped setups. Most customers choose the first for lower ops burden.

[16:00] Asha Rao: We're also evaluating competition — Anthropic's dedicated offering and a self-hosted Mistral stack. What would be the key Redwood differentiators for this pilot?
[16:10] Maya Chen: Production-first developer experience, built-in batching and caching with transparent cost dashboards, and unified rollouts across hosted/dedicated/private. Also our Optimize tool recommends quantization/batching params tailored to workload.

[17:45] Priya Singh: Ok, small nit: last time we tried quantization the quality regression on named-entity prompts was visible. How do you guard against regressions?
[17:55] Ravi Patel: We use prompt-based evals — we can run your golden set across model variants and monitor per-prompt deltas. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions and suggest fallbacks.

[19:20] Jared Kim: For the pricing spreadsheet — can you show both committed and burst pricing? We want to model worst-case monthly spend.
[19:30] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll include committed baseline, burst credits, and an example cost model for a 3x promotional peak.

[21:00] Marco Silva: What about integration with our SSO (Okta) and RBAC for token-level access?
[21:10] Elena Ortiz: We support SAML SSO (Okta), SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC workspaces with token scoping. We'll share the implementation guide.

[22:45] Sofia Alvarez: One more reliability question — how does Redwood handle graceful degradation if a model variant becomes overloaded?
[22:55] Tom Bowers: We have automated fallback policies: route to a lower-cost, smaller model variant, or route to cached responses while flagging for human-in-loop. Fallbacks are policy configurable per-route.

[24:00] Priya Singh: Are there any constraints on model size for Dedicated pools? We run a 30B model for recommendations.
[24:10] Ravi Patel: Dedicated supports a range of model sizes; kernel selection and multi-GPU sharding are handled by the runtime. For 30B we typically recommend multi-GPU sharded nodes with continuous KV cache management. We'll propose exact capacity in the pilot plan.

[26:30] Jared Kim: Let's talk timeline: We want pilot agreed and started by mid-August to validate before our September big campaign. Is that feasible?
[26:40] Maya Chen: Feasible. Action items: get us the traces by 7/26, Redwood shares pricing by 7/28, benchmark plan by 7/30, we aim to provision Dedicated pilot by the week of 8/10 and run shadow week + active week before 9/1.

[28:50] Priya Singh: About instrumentation — what metrics should we expect in the console? We need per-route latency percentiles, cost per token, autoscale events, and tracing to correlate model calls to front-end events.
[29:02] Tom Bowers: The console exposes per-route p50/p95/p99, token counts, cost breakdown, batching stats, and trace links you can hook into Jaeger/Zipkin. We can also publish custom logs to your logging endpoint.

[31:30] Marco Silva: If during the pilot we see unacceptable quality regression on quantized model, what's the rollback cadence?
[31:40] Ravi Patel: We recommend canary rollouts with automatic rollback thresholds. If regression exceeds NPS or a defined metric, the system automatically rolls back and notifies operators.

[33:10] Asha Rao: Okay, governance question: who signs off on production launch for Dedicated? Is that an AE/SE handoff to CSM plus our SRE signoff?
[33:20] Elena Ortiz: Typically AE/SE deliver pilot results; CSM coordinates the SRE and security signoff. We'll help with runbooks and run a production readiness checklist.

[34:40] Priya Singh: Small practical — does Redwood provide a cost simulator we can plug our traffic into?
[34:50] Maya Chen: Yes we have a cost simulator, but we'll send a customized spreadsheet modeling your traffic and the expected unit costs across tiers.

[36:00] Marco Silva: Let's surface a few risk items: tokenization deltas, audit log retention limits, and surge headroom. Can you address retention and headroom in the packet?
[36:10] Elena Ortiz: We'll include retention options (30/90/365 days) and recommended burst headroom sizing for your peak multiplier.

[38:00] Jared Kim: If we agree to Dedicated for promos, will Redwood help with code changes like adding prefix caching hooks? We don't want to touch production code too much.
[38:10] Ravi Patel: We can provide SDK patches and wrappers you can drop in; most customers use the prefix cache as a thin middleware layer. The SE team can help during the shadow week.

[40:05] Sofia Alvarez: Ok, about the benchmark — what two metrics should we prioritize? Latency SLO and cost per 1M requests?
[40:15] Tom Bowers: Yes, prioritize p99 latency and $/1M requests for the primary route, and accuracy delta on the golden set as the quality gate.

[42:20] Priya Singh: For the golden set, we'll share ~500 labeled cases for the team to run. Are there format constraints?
[42:30] Ravi Patel: CSV or JSONL with columns: prompt, expected_labels, tolerances. We'll run evals and produce per-prompt diffs.

[44:05] Maya Chen: Great — putting that all together, our deliverables: pricing sheet (Maya), benchmark plan (Ravi), security/compliance pack (Elena), you provide traces and golden set (HoloMart), schedule pilot provisioning for week of 8/10.

[45:10] Marco Silva: Sounds good. Quick question: if we need regional isolation in EU, is Dedicated available in eu-west-1?
[45:20] Tom Bowers: Yes, we have EU regions; we'll show a latency map and region cost delta in the pricing.

[46:50] Asha Rao: Anything else on governance? We want to include legal review for the pilot T&Cs.
[46:58] Maya Chen: We'll include a pilot agreement template; legal can do a quick review.

[48:10] Priya Singh: On the subject of observability, can you export raw token-level logs or just aggregates?
[48:20] Elena Ortiz: By default aggregates for cost reasons, but we can configure token-level logs for a retention-limited window for debugging. We'll note compliance implications.

[50:00] Jared Kim: Ok let's recap next steps quickly.
[50:05] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) HoloMart provides 7-day traffic trace and 500-case golden set by 7/26 (Sofia + Priya + Jared). 2) Redwood sends pilot pricing by 7/28 (Maya). 3) Benchmark plan by 7/30 (Ravi). 4) Security/compliance packet by 7/29 (Elena). 5) Pilot provisioning week of 8/10 with shadow -> active run, follow-up QBR on 8/20.
[51:00] Marco Silva: OK, we accept that plan. Thanks everyone.
[51:10] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll send notes and the spreadsheet after the call.
[51:20] Elena Ortiz: I'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark windows.
[51:30] Tom Bowers: Thanks all.

[51:40] End of recording.
